tools.hash-generator.faqs.0.question: What is a hash generator?
tools.hash-generator.faqs.0.answer: A hash generator is a tool that converts input text into a fixed-length string. Hashes are one-way — you cannot reverse a hash back into the original text. They are used for data integrity, password storage and digital signatures.
tools.hash-generator.faqs.1.question: Which hash algorithms are supported?
tools.hash-generator.faqs.1.answer: The tool supports SHA-1, SHA-256, SHA-384 and SHA-512. SHA-256 and SHA-512 are recommended for secure applications. SHA-1 is no longer recommended for security reasons but may be used for legacy systems.
tools.hash-generator.faqs.2.question: How do I generate a hash?
tools.hash-generator.faqs.2.answer: Type or paste text into the input field. Select the desired hash algorithm. The hash is generated and displayed immediately. Click copy to copy it to your clipboard.
tools.hash-generator.faqs.3.question: Are the hashes secure?
tools.hash-generator.faqs.3.answer: SHA-256 and SHA-512 are currently considered secure. SHA-1 has known collision vulnerabilities and should not be used for security purposes. For password hashing, use dedicated functions such as bcrypt or Argon2.
tools.hash-generator.faqs.4.question: Can I hash files?
tools.hash-generator.faqs.4.answer: The current version only supports text input. For file hashing, you need to read the file contents and pass them as text.
tools.hash-generator.faqs.5.question: Is hashing safe in the browser?
tools.hash-generator.faqs.5.answer: Yes. All hashing is done in the browser using the native Web Crypto API. No data is sent to any server.

tools.html-entity-encoder.faqs.0.answer: HTML entities are codes used to display reserved characters or characters that are not easy to type on a keyboard in HTML. For example, < becomes <, > becomes >, and & becomes &.
tools.html-entity-encoder.faqs.1.questio: How do I encode HTML entities?
tools.html-entity-encoder.faqs.1.answer: Paste your text into the input field. Select the encode mode. The tool converts special characters into HTML entities.
tools.html-entity-encoder.faqs.2.questio: How do I decode HTML entities?
tools.html-entity-encoder.faqs.2.answer: Paste text containing HTML entities into the input field. Select the decode mode. The tool converts the entities back into their original characters.
tools.html-entity-encoder.faqs.3.questio: Why do I need to encode HTML entities?
tools.html-entity-encoder.faqs.3.answer: Some characters have special meaning in HTML (like < and > for tags). To display them on a page, they must be encoded as entities, otherwise the browser interprets them as HTML.
tools.html-entity-encoder.faqs.4.questio: What is the difference between named and numeric entities?
tools.html-entity-encoder.faqs.4.answer: Named entities use names (like <), while numeric entities use character codes (like <). They are equivalent, but named entities are easier to read.
tools.html-entity-encoder.faqs.5.answer: Yes. This tool encodes and decodes HTML entities locally in the browser. No data is sent to any server.

tools.html-minifier.faqs.0.question: What is HTML minification?
tools.html-minifier.faqs.0.answer: HTML minification reduces the size of an HTML file by removing unnecessary whitespace, comments and optionally inlining CSS/JavaScript. This can improve page load speed and reduce bandwidth usage.
tools.html-minifier.faqs.1.question: How do I minify HTML?
tools.html-minifier.faqs.1.answer: Paste your HTML code into the input field. Click the minify button. The tool removes whitespace and comments to produce a smaller output. Copy the result or download the minified file.
tools.html-minifier.faqs.2.question: Does minification affect HTML functionality?
tools.html-minifier.faqs.2.answer: No. Minification only removes characters that are unnecessary for rendering. The functionality and appearance of your HTML remain unchanged. However, it may make the code harder to read or debug.
tools.html-minifier.faqs.3.question: How much can minification reduce file size?
tools.html-minifier.faqs.3.answer: The reduction depends on the original HTML. Files with lots of whitespace and comments can be reduced by 50-80%. Already compact HTML may see only a small reduction.
tools.html-minifier.faqs.4.question: Is my HTML sent to a server?
tools.html-minifier.faqs.4.answer: No. All minification happens locally in your browser. The code never leaves your device.
tools.html-minifier.faqs.5.question: Can I minify large HTML files?
tools.html-minifier.faqs.5.answer: Yes. Since minification happens in the browser, it can handle large HTML files. However, very large files (>50 MB) may be slow due to browser memory limits.

tools.json-to-csv.faqs.1.question: What format should the JSON be in?
tools.json-to-csv.faqs.1.answer: The JSON should be an array of objects. Each object represents a row, and the keys become the column headers. For example: [{"name":"John","age":30},{"name":"Jane","age":25}].
tools.json-to-csv.faqs.2.question: Can it handle nested JSON?
tools.json-to-csv.faqs.2.answer: The current version supports flat objects. Nested objects are converted to string representations. For deeply nested JSON, it is recommended to flatten the data before converting.
tools.json-to-csv.faqs.3.question: Can the CSV output be opened in spreadsheet software?

tools.jwt-decoder.metadata.description: Decode and inspect JSON Web Tokens (JWT), with signature verification support
tools.jwt-decoder.faqs.0.question: What is a JWT?
tools.jwt-decoder.faqs.0.answer: A JWT (JSON Web Token) is a compact, URL-safe format for representing claims between parties. It consists of three parts — header, payload and signature — encoded in Base64URL and separated by dots (.).
tools.jwt-decoder.faqs.1.question: How do I decode a JWT?
tools.jwt-decoder.faqs.1.answer: Paste the JWT into the input field. The tool decodes it automatically and displays the header and payload parts in a readable format. It also checks whether the token has expired.
tools.jwt-decoder.faqs.2.question: Can this tool verify JWT signatures?
tools.jwt-decoder.faqs.2.answer: No. This tool only decodes JWTs without verifying the signature. Verification requires the key used to sign the token. Always verify JWTs on the server side.
tools.jwt-decoder.faqs.3.question: Are JWTs secure?
tools.jwt-decoder.faqs.3.answer: JWTs can be used securely, but must be implemented correctly. Always verify the signature, check the expiration time, do not store sensitive data in the payload (it is Base64 encoded, not encrypted), and use HTTPS in transit.
tools.jwt-decoder.faqs.4.question: What are common use cases for JWTs?
tools.jwt-decoder.faqs.4.answer: JWTs are commonly used for authentication (after login, the server returns a JWT that the client stores), information exchange (securely transferring information between parties) and authorization (representing user permissions).
tools.jwt-decoder.faqs.5.question: Is decoding a JWT safe?
tools.jwt-decoder.faqs.5.answer: Yes. This tool decodes JWTs locally in the browser. No data is sent to any server. However, do not store sensitive information in client-side JWTs, because anyone can decode them.

tools.meta-tag-generator.faqs.0.question: What are meta tags?
tools.meta-tag-generator.faqs.0.answer: Meta tags are tags in the head of an HTML document that provide metadata about the page, such as the title, description, keywords and Open Graph information. They are not displayed on the page but are used by search engines and social media platforms.
tools.meta-tag-generator.faqs.1.question: How do I use the meta tag generator?
tools.meta-tag-generator.faqs.1.answer: Fill in the form fields: title, description, keywords, image and so on. The tool generates the HTML meta tags in real time. Copy the generated code and paste it into the <head> section of your HTML.
tools.meta-tag-generator.faqs.2.question: What are Open Graph tags?
tools.meta-tag-generator.faqs.2.answer: Open Graph tags control how your page appears when shared on Facebook, LinkedIn and other social platforms. They define the title, description, image and other elements shown when sharing.
tools.meta-tag-generator.faqs.3.question: What are Twitter card tags?
tools.meta-tag-generator.faqs.3.answer: Twitter card tags control how your page appears when shared on Twitter. They are similar to Open Graph tags but specific to Twitter, and can enable special formats such as large images or app install cards.
tools.meta-tag-generator.faqs.4.question: Are meta tags important for SEO?
tools.meta-tag-generator.faqs.4.answer: Yes. While meta keywords no longer directly affect rankings, meta titles and descriptions are important for SEO. They appear in search results and can influence click-through rates. Open Graph tags also affect social sharing.
tools.meta-tag-generator.faqs.5.question: Can I generate tags for multiple platforms?
tools.meta-tag-generator.faqs.5.answer: Yes. The generator creates standard meta tags, Open Graph tags (for Facebook, LinkedIn, etc.) and Twitter card tags. All tags are included in the generated code.

tools.robots-txt-generator.faqs.0.answer: robots.txt is a text file placed in the root directory of a website. It tells search engine crawlers which pages or files may or may not be crawled on your website.
tools.robots-txt-generator.faqs.1.questi: How do I use the robots.txt generator?
tools.robots-txt-generator.faqs.1.answer: Select the crawlers to allow (such as Googlebot, Bingbot), add allow and disallow rules, and specify the sitemap location. The tool generates a robots.txt file for you to download or copy.
tools.robots-txt-generator.faqs.2.questi: What is the difference between Disallow and Allow directives?
tools.robots-txt-generator.faqs.2.answer: Disallow tells crawlers not to access specific paths. Allow overrides Disallow and permits access to specific sub-paths. By default, everything is allowed if no rules are specified.
tools.robots-txt-generator.faqs.3.answer: Usually not. You generally only want to block specific directories (like /admin/ or /private/). Blocking all crawlers (User-agent: * Disallow: /) removes your website from search results.
tools.robots-txt-generator.faqs.4.answer: No. robots.txt is publicly accessible and anyone can read it. It does not prevent users from accessing pages. For real protection, use password protection or server-side authentication.
tools.robots-txt-generator.faqs.5.questi: Should I include a Sitemap directive?
tools.robots-txt-generator.faqs.5.answer: Yes. Including Sitemap: https://example.com/sitemap.xml helps search engines find your sitemap and index your website better.
tools.robots-txt-generator.guide.intro.p: A robots.txt generator is a free online tool for creating robots.txt files. It helps you control how search engine crawlers interact with your website, specify which paths are allowed or disallowed, and include sitemap references. All generation happens in the browser.
tools.robots-txt-generator.guide.section: Select the crawler to configure (or use * for all crawlers). Add allow and disallow rules to specify which paths may or may not be crawled. Add your sitemap URL. Copy the generated robots.txt content and upload it to the root directory of your website.

robots.txt uses the User-agent directive to specify which crawler a rule applies to. The Disallow directive blocks access to paths. The Allow directive overrides Disallow. The Sitemap directive specifies the sitemap location.

tools.timestamp-converter.metadata.title: Timestamp Converter
tools.timestamp-converter.metadata.descr: Convert between Unix timestamps and human-readable dates
tools.timestamp-converter.faqs.0.answer: A Unix timestamp is the number of seconds elapsed since January 1, 1970 00:00:00 UTC (known as the "epoch"). It is a standard way to represent time in computer systems and programming.
tools.timestamp-converter.faqs.1.questio: How do I convert a timestamp to a date?
tools.timestamp-converter.faqs.1.answer: Enter the Unix timestamp in the timestamp field. The tool instantly converts it to a human-readable date and time, displayed in your local timezone and UTC.
tools.timestamp-converter.faqs.2.questio: How do I convert a date to a timestamp?
tools.timestamp-converter.faqs.2.answer: Pick a date and time with the date picker or enter it manually. The tool generates the corresponding Unix timestamp.
tools.timestamp-converter.faqs.3.questio: Are timestamps in seconds or milliseconds?
tools.timestamp-converter.faqs.3.answer: The tool shows both second (10-digit) and millisecond (13-digit) timestamps. Most systems use seconds, but JavaScript's Date.now() returns milliseconds.
tools.timestamp-converter.faqs.4.answer: The current timestamp is shown at the top of the tool and updates in real time every second. It displays the current Unix time in seconds and milliseconds.
tools.timestamp-converter.faqs.5.answer: Timestamps are always based on UTC. The converted date is displayed in both your local timezone and UTC for easy reference.
tools.timestamp-converter.guide.intro.ti: What is a Unix Timestamp Converter?
tools.timestamp-converter.guide.intro.pa: A Unix timestamp converter is a free online tool for converting between Unix timestamps and human-readable dates. It also shows the live current timestamp. All conversions happen in the browser.
tools.timestamp-converter.guide.sections: How to convert a timestamp to a date
Enter the Unix timestamp in the timestamp field. The tool instantly displays the corresponding date and time, formatted in your local timezone and UTC.
How to convert a date to a timestamp
Pick a date and time with the date picker or enter it manually. The tool generates the corresponding Unix timestamp in seconds and milliseconds.
Unix time (also called epoch time) is the number of seconds elapsed since January 1, 1970 00:00:00 UTC. It ignores leap seconds and has exactly 86400 seconds per day.
